annotations.summary: Backlog refills failed three times in the last hour.
annotations.description: Counted from the error each failed try logs, whichever refill it was for: one refill's three tries (ten minutes apart), or failures of separate refills (after publishing, Summon). Either way refills keep failing, and a single passing failure doesn't alert. The logs say why: a model, Jev or Cosmos DB. The backlog shrinks by one a day until refills work again; Summon New Rites in the Scriptorium tries again.

annotations.summary: Publishing found the backlog empty more than once this week.
annotations.description: Counted from the warning DailyRitePublisher logs each time. Each time, the day's rite was written on the spot, unmoderated. Refills aren't keeping up: check the Refills failing alert, and summon new rites in the Scriptorium.

annotations.summary: Two or more drafts in the last day couldn't be judged.
annotations.description: Counted from the warning BacklogRefiller logs for each draft Jev couldn't judge; one can be a passing blip, a second in a day isn't (a refill after publishing writes about one draft a day). The drafts still join the backlog, but without a quality or scores, so the Augury puts them last and More rites falls back to the newest. The warnings say why: an expired Jev key, or Jev down.

annotations.summary: More than 5% of production's requests failed (5xx) for ten minutes.
annotations.description: Only counted over at least ten requests in ten minutes, so one failure on a quiet night doesn't alert. A counter's first value in a new process isn't counted, but errors that last ten minutes come many to a process. The dashboard's Traffic row shows which function; its error logs say why (often Cosmos DB).

model.expr: sum(increase(probe_all_success_sum{job="Daily Machine Spirit Today"}[15m])) / sum(increase(probe_all_success_count{job="Daily Machine Spirit Today"}[15m]))

annotations.summary: More than half of the last 15 minutes' checks of Today failed, for five minutes.
annotations.description: Synthetic Monitoring's check (Daily Machine Spirit Today, observability/synthetics/todays-rite.js) loads Today through Cloudflare, as readers do, every five minutes from two probes. It fails when Today doesn't answer 200, when Cloudflare served a STALE copy because the app didn't answer (readers still see the site, read-only), or when Today doesn't show today's rite after 01:30 UTC. The check's own logs in Synthetic Monitoring say which. No data means the check was paused or deleted: run tools/grafana-synthetics.ps1.

annotations.summary: Production has sent no telemetry for 26 hours.
annotations.description: The app sleeps when nobody visits, but the DailyRite timer wakes it every midnight, so a day of silence means the export is broken (the OtlpHeaders token, revoked or read-only) or the app is down. Every other alert is blind until this is fixed.
